killedBy: runs.mjs: removing the AudioContext constructor before boot installs the override on the workload context, unconditionally, before it navigates
why: Leaves the two real `AudioContext`s the app builds at boot -- Howler's, when `createAudioEngine` first touches `Howler.volume()`, and `engine.ts`'s `ensureCtx`. On a host whose audio service never connects each constructor returns only after an internal 20-second timeout, so the page blocks for ~40 s before `load` fires and the frame-time benchmark measures a page that spent ~40 s in an audio constructor before `load`. Worse than a failure: a run that survives the timeout reports numbers shaped by the stall.
